subject: Centering matters when fitting state-space models in Stan?

messages.author: 528560773e2cb27f
messages.subject: Centering matters when fitting state-space models in Stan?
parts:
Hi all,

I've been trying to fit a state-space model of the vector time-series in RStan. I had two variables, y1 and y2, where y2 was centered to mean zero but y1 was not for some reason. I found that with such data Stan does not start sampling and shows the following error message:

    No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?

but it works when y1 was centered. I guess there should be something wrong in my code but I couldn't identify it. The data/inits dump file and model file are attached. I would appreciate any help on this.

Regards,
Keiichi

P.S.
I've tried to fit several models (a state-space model with multi_normal distributions/ a standard random wark model with a multi_normal distribution/ a standard multi_normal model/ a state_space model with normal distributions) to same data but this problem occurs only when I fitted state-space models. Attached files are the code for the state-space model with multi_normal distributions and associating data/inits, but if someone needs other models and their data/inits I can share them as well.

----
Keiichi FUKAYA, Ph.D.
Faculty of Environmental Science
Hokkaido University

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Centering matters when fitting state-space models in Stan?

On 9/27/12 10:26 PM, FUKAYA Keiichi wrote:
> Hi all,

> I've been trying to fit a state-space model of the vector time-series in RStan. I had two variables, y1 and y2, where y2
> was centered to mean zero but y1 was not for some reason. I found that with such data Stan does not start sampling and
> shows the following error message:
>
> No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?
>
> but it works when y1 was centered. I guess there should be something wrong in my code but I couldn't identify it. The
> data/inits dump file and model file are attached. I would appreciate any help on this.
>
> Regards,
> Keiichi
>
> P.S.
> I've tried to fit several models (a state-space model with multi_normal distributions/ a standard random wark model with
> a multi_normal distribution/ a standard multi_normal model/ a state_space model with normal distributions) to same data
> but this problem occurs only when I fitted state-space models. Attached files are the code for the state-space model
> with multi_normal distributions and associating data/inits, but if someone needs other models and their data/inits I can
> share them as well.

Thanks for the clear error report -- it really helps
to have everything at hand.

I don't know anything about state-space models, but it
looks like a pretty straightforward time-series arrangement.

Your problem is probably related to the uniform
samples for t=1. Because y_dash[1,n] is a parameter, there's nothing
keeping it bounded between min_y[n] and max_y[n]. The uniform
doesn't do that -- it only evaluates the probability.
If it gets out of bounds, you'll run into the problem
you see because no step size is small enough to move
out of a point not in the support of the probability function.

For now, I'd suggest option 1:

1. get rid of the uniform sampling for t=1. If the
y_dash[1,n] stay in range, it doesn't do anything because
we only compute probabilities up to a proportion and
so there's no contribution from a uniform with constant
bounds.

You could also try option 2:

2. declare in the parameters block that y_dash[1,n] is
bounded between min_y[n] and max_y[n]. Unfortunately, we
haven't yet added bounds constraints to vectors and matrices,
and even wehn we do, it's not going to support declaring each
entry in a data structure to have different bounds. So for
now, you'd have to:

a. fix an overall bound for the y_dash not dependent on n

b. declare a 2D array with those bounds

c. copy the entries into a transformed parameter vector

I'm about to add the code that'll let you declare a bound
directly, but even then, it won't support varying bounds on
different components of the structure.

You can diagnose some of these problems using the test_grad
option Jiqiang added to RStan in 1.0.2. It'll dump all
the unconstrained params and their gradients at the init
point. If the initial state's
illegal, you'll see NaN or infinite values.

I'm out of town now, but can look at this in more detail
next week when I get back if nobody else gets there first.

- Bob

messages.author: 528560773e2cb27f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Centering matters when fitting state-space models in Stan?
parts:
Hi Bob,

thank you very much for the detailed comments -- they were very
helpful and let me notice how the Stan code can be different from that
in WinBUGS (in WinBUGS I think priors should be specified for t = 1
and they would keep parameters bounded).

The option 1 you suggested fixed the problem. Also, letting min_y very
small and max_y very large worked as well (although this should not be
a smart solution, it made me confident what you explained was
correct).

Regards,
Keiichi

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Centering matters when fitting state-space models in Stan?
parts:
On Sat, Sep 29, 2012 at 10:19 PM, Jeffrey Arnold
<jeffrey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Bob,
>
> Does log_uniform() return -Inf if the value is outside the support of the
> distribution?

Hi Jeffrey,

uniform_log() currently throws an exception if the value is outside
the support of the distribution. We are in the process of working
through all the distributions so they return -Inf when outside the
support of the distribution.

In Stan, under most situations, both behaviors results in rejecting
the sample. The way it is currently implemented, it will produce a
non-fatal error message. Once we change the behavior, the error
message will disappear.


Daniel
